page.title: Half Awake
page.posterTitle: A Within-Brain Comparison of Aperiodic and Oscillatory EEG During Unilateral Methohexital Anesthesia
page.subtitle: Primary bipolar EEG analysis of a rare within-participant hemispheric perturbation
page.description: Half Awake examines aperiodic and oscillatory EEG changes during unilateral methohexital anesthesia using a standard-bipolar, within-participant hemispheric contrast.
page.socialDescription: A primary standard-bipolar analysis of aperiodic and oscillatory EEG during unilateral methohexital anesthesia.
page.socialImageAlt: Half Awake title card describing a primary bipolar EEG analysis of a within-participant hemispheric perturbation.

takeaway.statement: In a sample of 27 participants, the standard-bipolar aperiodic exponent showed a positive injected-minus-contralateral interaction.
takeaway.note: The mean interaction was 0.245 exponent units (95% CI 0.043–0.447; raw two-sided p=.019) in the primary standard-bipolar analysis.
takeaway.calibration: Following injection, exponent steepening was consistently greater in the injected hemisphere than in the contralateral hemisphere—a statistically significant difference (raw two-sided p=.019) supporting a localized anesthetic effect rather than a bilateral recording artifact.

scientificLogic.title: Unilateral anesthesia
scientificLogic.description: Methohexital is administered through one carotid artery to produce temporary, predominantly unilateral cerebral anesthesia.

scientificLogic.title: Two conditions
scientificLogic.description: EEG is compared between baseline and anesthesia within each hemisphere of the same participant.

scientificLogic.title: Two hemispheres
scientificLogic.description: Baseline-to-anesthesia change is estimated separately for the injected and contralateral sides.

scientificLogic.title: Difference of differences
scientificLogic.description: The contralateral change is subtracted from the injected-side change to test for a lateralized interaction.

scientificLogic.title: Candidate features
scientificLogic.description: The same bipolar contrast is applied to aperiodic exponent, theta peak strength, and descriptive aperiodic offset.

withinBrainDesign: Each participant contributes baseline and anesthesia measurements from both hemispheres. The principal interaction is [(anesthesia − baseline) injected] − [(anesthesia − baseline) contralateral]. The contralateral hemisphere is a simultaneous within-participant comparator, not an untreated or unaffected control.

researchQuestion.introduction: Does the aperiodic EEG exponent change more after unilateral methohexital administration in the injected hemisphere than in the contralateral hemisphere, and does oscillatory theta peak strength show the same pattern?

points.title: A rare natural experiment
points.text: The Wada procedure temporarily perturbs one hemisphere while EEG is recorded from both sides, enabling a within-participant comparison.

points.title: A challenging clinical signal
points.text: Movement, muscle activity, arousal, and behavioral testing can create broadband changes that are shared across hemispheres.

points.title: Background and peaks
points.text: Spectral parameterization separates the aperiodic background from detected oscillatory peaks instead of treating every power shift as rhythmic activity.

points.title: Lateralization, not an untreated control
points.text: The injected-minus-contralateral interaction asks whether change follows the injected side; it does not assume the other hemisphere is unaffected.

methods.label: Clinical context
methods.title: Wada procedure
methods.summary: Methohexital is administered through one carotid artery to produce temporary, predominantly unilateral cerebral anesthesia while EEG is recorded from both hemispheres.

methods.label: Signal preparation
methods.title: EEG preprocessing
methods.summary: A fixed 23-channel scalp set is retained after Fp1, Fp2, and nonstandard channels are removed. Supported 512-Hz recordings are resampled to 256 Hz; continuous data are demeaned, linearly detrended, and high-pass filtered at 0.5 Hz.

methods.label: Quality control
methods.title: Artifact handling
methods.summary: Four-second epochs are flagged using robust and absolute peak-to-peak amplitude criteria and then manually reviewed in an additional artifact-review step. Manually curated baseline and anesthesia recordings require at least 50 seconds per condition.

methods.label: Primary montage
methods.title: Standard bipolar signals
methods.summary: A predefined 12-pair bipolar montage is derived from cleaned continuous data before epoch construction. Each signal is the first electrode minus the second, and pair laterality is aligned to the injected side.

methods.label: Primary region
methods.title: Tier-1 bipolar ROI
methods.summary: The primary parasagittal region uses F3–C3 and C3–P3 on the left and F4–C4 and C4–P4 on the right. The injection side determines which pair set is labeled injected or contralateral.

methods.label: Analysis windows
methods.title: Paired accepted segments
methods.summary: The source baseline spans up to 180 seconds before injection and ends 10 seconds before it; anesthesia source data begin 15 seconds after injection. Accepted whole segments are accumulated toward a 100-second target without splitting boundary segments.

methods.label: Spectral estimator
methods.title: Multitaper spectra
methods.summary: FieldTrip DPSS multitaper spectra use 2-Hz smoothing, a 0.5-Hz frequency grid, and 180-second padding. Spectra are estimated per accepted segment and averaged in linear power using segment duration as the weight.

methods.label: Spectral model
methods.title: Aperiodic and periodic features
methods.summary: Fixed-mode FOOOF fitting separates aperiodic exponent and offset from detected peaks. Fits use 2–35 Hz or 2–25 Hz according to acquisition hardware, with theta defined as the strongest accepted peak from 4–8 Hz.

methods.label: Primary inference
methods.title: Within-participant group test
methods.summary: The primary exponent result uses a two-sided paired t test of the injected-minus-contralateral interaction. The displayed p-value is raw, and the saved aggregate result does not provide a standardized effect size.

results.label: Primary analysis · standard bipolar
results.title: Aperiodic exponent showed an injected-side interaction
results.statement: After anesthesia, the aperiodic exponent increased more on the injected side than on the contralateral side in the standard-bipolar analysis.
results.metric: N=27 · mean interaction=0.245 · 95% CI 0.043–0.447 · t(26)=2.49 · raw two-sided p=.019
results.analysisPlan: The primary result is a two-sided paired t test of the injected-minus-contralateral interaction; the displayed p-value is raw and no standardized effect size is available in the saved aggregate result.
results.interpretation: The primary bipolar analysis supports a positive lateralized exponent change.

results.label: Oscillatory comparison
results.title: Theta did not show the same interaction
results.statement: Theta peak strength changed little on either side and did not show evidence of an injected-versus-contralateral difference.
results.metric: N=27 · mean interaction=−0.0042 · raw two-sided p=.852 · confidence interval not available
results.analysisPlan: Theta was evaluated as a comparison endpoint using the same injected-minus-contralateral logic; its saved aggregate result does not include a confidence interval.
results.interpretation: The current cohort does not provide statistical evidence for a theta peak-strength interaction.
results.caution: An injected-side theta peak was detected in only 6 of 27 participants, and nondetection is encoded as zero.

results.label: Descriptive broadband feature
results.title: Aperiodic offset showed a positive direction
results.statement: The bipolar aperiodic offset had a positive average injected-minus-contralateral interaction.
results.metric: N=27 · mean interaction=0.721 · SD=0.478 · 26 positive / 1 negative · no inferential p-value
results.analysisPlan: Offset was summarized descriptively; no current hypothesis test, confidence interval, or multiplicity correction is available.
results.interpretation: The direction is notable as a descriptive broadband-power pattern, not as confirmed statistical evidence.

results.label: Descriptive signal availability
results.title: Exponent estimates were more consistently available
results.statement: By the nature of the aperiodic fit, a spectral exponent is available as a measurable metric for every fitted participant, whereas theta availability depends on whether the peak-detection rule identifies a peak.
results.metric: N=27 · exponent fits=27/27 · injected-side theta detected=6/27 · descriptive only
results.analysisPlan: Availability was summarized descriptively; the exponent's lateralization was tested separately using the injected-minus-contralateral interaction.
results.interpretation: The exponent was tested to determine whether it lateralized with the injected-side pharmacodynamics of methohexital.
results.caution: Availability alone does not imply that the metric is meaningful. Therefore, we tested whether the baseline-to-anesthesia change in aperiodic spectral exponent differed between the injected and contralateral hemispheres during the Wada procedure, and applied the same lateralized interaction test to theta peak strength.
